population: H1: existing individual iOS accounts in Japan; Japanese L1; English course around B1.1; actual speaking level separately screened
excluded: new registrations; family subscriptions; already-covered Super accounts for P1; already-entitled Free accounts for P2
numeric_basis: All economic numbers below are authored D examples, not estimates, tariffs, actual plan prices, probabilities of scenarios, or data-calibrated bounds. USD is a common accounting unit only.
path_basis: Each bin represents a complete H-period billing path with assumed mean contribution after refunds and necessary non-AI variable fees. Equal path contributions and non-offer billable workload across arms are additional D assumptions; endpoint tier alone would not establish these values.
cost_basis: Service minute is an illustrative all-pipeline workload unit, not learner speaking time. Offer attempts (including failed attempts/retries) and non-offer paid-entitlement workload are disjoint tags. No extra retry multiplier is used. Actual audio/token/provider mix remains unknown.

P0.definition: Maintain each account's audited current rights; current account-level rights not verified. Relative delta is zero, not zero absolute operating cost.

P1.definition: Only originally Super and audited not eligible for Lily under P0: add at most 24 attempts over H. Stop this policy branch if no genuine entitlement increment exists. Original Max spillover is separate, hypothetical.

P2.definition: Only originally Free and audited not already trial-entitled: first 14 days at most 4 attempts; close at expiry; no automatic charge. Post-purchase paid workload over H is separately included.

low.label: D low response intensity; not a pessimistic forecast

base.label: D reference response intensity; not most likely

high.label: D high response intensity; higher use can lower net value

sensitivity.basis: D scan values, not empirical bounds; reference offer workload held fixed; paid-path workload changes with gain/loss. No probabilities or confidence intervals. No real-world robust ranking.
